html.body: Date: 2025-03-19 REMARKSClaims 1-20 were and remain pending in the application. By this paper, claims 1, 6, 11, and 16 have been amended. No claims have been added or canceled. No new matter is added.Support for the amendments to the claims can be found, for example, in paragraphs [0006] and [0101], claim 6 as originally presented, and Figure 5 as filed. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are hereby respectfully requested in view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks.Claim Rejections - 35 U.S.C. §103 Claims 1-3, 8, 10-13, 18, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as obvious over U.S.Patent Document No. 2021/0383209 ("Brahma") in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,782,451 ("Venkatraman"). Claims 2, 3, 8, and 10 depend from claim 1. Claims 12, 18, and 20 depend from claim 11.Claim 1, as amended, recites "wherein the second path is a driver's actual driving path." Brahma and Venkatraman do not teach or suggest this limitation.Brahma describes a method for training a model for an autonomous vehicle. See Brahman, abstract; paragraph [0003]. Brahma describes "a path planning system of the vehicle may determine, identify, generate, etc., a path for the vehicle based on objects detected by a perception system 1420 and estimated/predicted locations of the objects determined by the prediction system." See Brahma, paragraph [0083]. Brahma further describes "[a] first neural network model may generate the path 1605 illustrated in FIG. 6 for the vehicle" and "[t]he first neural network model may generate a line (e.g., the dotted line) to represent the path (e.g., vehicle path) along the road 1615 depicted in the image 1600." Accordingly, as described in Brahma, the first path 1605 is generated by a neural network model of path planning system and is not a driver's actual driving path. Additionally, paragraph [0060] of Brahma describes that "the path planning system 1440 may generate a path along a road that avoids one or more obstacles." See Brahma, paragraph [0060].Venkatraman fails to cure the deficiencies of Brahma. Venkatraman is cited for path generation at an intersection. See Office action, page 4. Venkatraman is not cited for and does not teach or suggest the aforementioned limitation of independent claim 1.For at least the foregoing reasons, the combination of Brahma and Venkatraman fails to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claim 1 as amended. Accordingly, amended claim 1 and corresponding dependent claims 2, 3, 8, and 10 are not rendered obvious by this cited reference combination.Independent claim 11 has been amended to include limitations substantially similar to those of independent claim 1. For at least the same reasons as described above with respect to claim 1, the combination of Brahma and Venkatraman fails to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claim 11 as amended. Accordingly, amended claim 11 and corresponding dependent claims 12, 18, and 20 are not rendered obvious by the cited reference combination for consistent reasons.Claims 1 and 11 are allowable for another reason. Claim 1 has been amended herein to include some limitations of dependent claim 6 and claim 11 has been amended herein to include some limitations of dependent claim 16. Dependent claims 6 and 16 were not rejected as obvious over Brahma and Venkatraman. Accordingly, it is believed that Brahma and Venkatraman fail to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claims 1 and 11 as amended. See below regarding the separate rejection of claims 6 and 16.Claims 4, 9, 14, and 19 are rejected as obvious over Brahma in view of Venkatraman and Chinese Patent Document No. CN 114184201 ("Xingjia"). Claims 4 and 9 depend from independent claim 1. Claims 14 and 19 depend from independent claim 11. The deficiencies in the teachings of Brahma and Venkatraman with respect to claims 1 and 11 are noted above.Xingjia fails to cure these deficiencies and has not been cited as doing so. Thus, the combination of Brahma, Venkatraman, and Xingjia fails to render obvious claims 1 and 11, and as a result, dependent claims 18 and 19 for at least the same reasons.Claims 5-7 and 15-17 are rejected as obvious over Brahma in view of Venkatraman, U.S.Patent Publication No. 2022/0082403 ("Shapira"), and U.S. Patent Publication No.2019/0071068 ("Shin"). Claims 5-7 depend from independent claim 1. Claims 15-17 depend from independent claim 11. Claims 1 and 11 have been amended herein to include some limitations of dependent claims 6 and 16, respectively. This rejection now applies to independent claims 1 and 11.Claim 1, as amended, recites "wherein the comparison operation storage is configured to store the information on the second path and the offset information in response to the offset information being smaller than a preset threshold, and wherein the autonomous driving apparatus is configured to learn the second path." Brahma and Venkatraman do not teach or suggest these limitations.Shapira describes systems and methods for mapping lanes for use in vehicle navigation.See Shapira, abstract. As described in Shapira, "target trajectory may represent an ideal path that a vehicle should take as the vehicle travels." See Shapira, paragraph [0219]. Shapira further describes:A road segment may be associated with a single target trajectory or multiple target trajectories. For example, on a two lane road, a first target trajectory may be stored to represent an intended path of travel along the road in a first direction, and a second target trajectory may be stored to represent an intended path of travel along the road in another direction (e.g., opposite to the first direction).Additional target trajectories may be stored with respect to a particular road segment. For example, on a multi-lane road one or more target trajectories may be stored representing intended paths of travel for vehicles in one or more lanes associated with the multi-lane road.See Shapira, paragraph [0218]. Accordingly, Shapira describes storing target trajectories, representing an ideal path that a vehicle should take as it travels, for example for each of multiple lanes included in a road. Additionally, Shapira describes:In some embodiments, each lane of a multi-lane road may be associated with its own target trajectory. In other embodiments, there may be fewer target trajectories stored than lanes present on a multi-lane road. In such cases, a vehicle navigating the multi-lane road may use any of the stored target trajectories to guides its navigation by taking into account an amount of lane offset from a lane for which a target trajectory is stored (e.g., if a vehicle is traveling in the left most lane of a three lane highway, and a target trajectory is stored only for the middle lane of the highway, the vehicle may navigate using the target trajectory of the middle lane by accounting for the amount of lane offset between the middle lane and the left-most lane when generating navigational instructions).See Shapira, paragraph [0218]. Accordingly, Shapira describes that if a target trajectory is stored for one, but not all lanes of a road, the vehicle may travel along the lane for which a target trajectory is not stored using the stored target trajectory of another lane and an offset (e.g., corresponding to a lane width and the number of lanes between the lane for which a target trajectory is not stored, on which the vehicle travels and the lane for which a target trajectory is stored). Futher, Shapira describes "navigation based on the target trajectory may include a determined amount of offset to be maintained relative to the location of the target trajectory." See Shapira, paragraph [0219].Shapira is completely silent as to storing information on a second path along which the autonomous vehicle is driving. Further, Shapira is completely silent as to a "preset threshold" and a comparison between the offset information and a preset threshold. The offset as described in Shapira is a known value corresponding to the width of a lane used to for driving when a target trajectory is not stored for a lane along which the vehicle is traveling. Shapira is further silent as to an "autonomous driving apparatus... configured to learn the second path" as recited by claim 1.Shin fails to cure the deficiencies of Brahma, Venkatraman, and Shapira. Shin is not cited for and does not teach or suggest the aforementioned limitation of independent claim 1.For at least the foregoing reasons, the combination of Brahma, Venkatraman, Shapira, and Shin fails to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claim 1 as amended. Accordingly, amended claim 1 and corresponding dependent claims 5-7 are not rendered obvious by this cited reference combination.Independent claim 11 has been amended to include limitations substantially similar to those of independent claim 1. For at least the same reasons as described above with respect to claim 1, the combination of Brahma, Venkatraman, Shapira, and Shin fails to teach or suggest one or more limitations of claim 11 as amended. Accordingly, amended claim 11 and corresponding dependent claims 15-17 are not rendered obvious by the cited reference combination for consistent reasons.The obviousness rejections are believed to be overcome.CONCLUSIONReconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are hereby respectfully solicited in view of the foregoing.The examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the telephone number listed below in order to discuss any remaining issues or matters of form that will place this case in condition for allowance.No fee is believed due at this time other than the above noted RCE fee.Respectfully submitted, /Anthony J.
